chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Fame — its good and its evil — is in the Fire.

key_terms.الشُّهْرَةُ: fame, notoriety, being widely known — here condemned as a spiritual vice regardless of whether it stems from good or evil deeds
key_terms.النَّارُ: the Fire, i.e., Hellfire — the ultimate consequence of insincerity and worldly vanity

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about seeking fame in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a sweeping condemnation of fame-seeking, declaring that all pursuit of notoriety — whether outwardly virtuous or openly vicious — leads to hellfire. This teaching reflects the foundational Islamic concern that sincerity (ikhlas) in worship and conduct must be entirely free of the desire for public recognition. The original audience would have understood 'al-shuhra' as the tendency to be conspicuous or talked about — a disposition seen in Shia ethics as incompatible with genuine devotion to God.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The fame (seeker), the good of it and the evil of it, are in the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Something that causes public abhorrence is in the fire, regardless of being good or bad.’”
